creator: Alexander Terp
description:
`rad check` is what you run to find out whether a script is sound before shipping it, and it currently certifies scripts that die on the first line that matters. Two shapes, one hole.

**Over-arity destructuring.** Index-first loop unpacking was removed in v0.7. Scripts written against the old semantics destructure wrongly under the new ones, produce wrong values, and pass `rad check` clean. Sites across three corpora: `epoch:23-24`, `argus:91,200,225,258` (two-element lists into three variables, a zip-of-five into six), `deplcr:30`, `platform-release:71`, `jerboa:32`, `pilot:12,24`, `feedmbean2:73`, `ssu:34,51,68`, `ssu2:33,55,69`, `argusp:24`, `replay:59`. Inferred statically - none was executed - but the arity mismatch is visible in the source. On `pilot`, check flags only the *downstream* type error; the semantic drift itself is invisible.

**Dead pre-v0.7 `for i, item in items`.** #153 batch 5 hit this directly: `rad check` says "No diagnostics to report", running says `RAD20033` with the migration hint. The checker already has the message - it just doesn't print it at check time.

The contrast that makes the case: `whale-cluster`'s use of the removed `get_default` sat in an equally dormant code path and *was* caught, because a removed function has a diagnostic and a wrong-arity destructure does not.

Two reasons this outranks its size. #153 batch 4 pitches running an older machine's `rad check` as the pre-ship version-skew check, and batch 5 undercuts that pitch three weeks later. And #153 notes where the habit comes from: old scripts on disk - the author's own pre-v0.7 version of the script being rewritten was sitting in the same directory.

---

### Orientation

- `rts/check/` owns both halves. The runtime already has the diagnostics; the checker simply never runs the equivalent test. `rts` must not import `core`.
- `rts/check/binder.go` resolves names and records `Resolved.ForLoopVars`; `rts/check/type_check.go` types expressions and distributes unpacks; `rts/check/check.go:78` `Check()` is the orchestration point listing every check that runs.
- Diagnostics reach the user as a `BindIssue` through `rts/check/check.go:154` `addBindIssues` or as a `TypeInfo.Issues` entry through `rts/check/check.go:122` `addTypeIssues`.

### Where to start

- **Dead pre-v0.7 `for i, item in items`.** Reproduced against `bin/radd` v0.11.0: `rad check` prints "No diagnostics to report" and running the same file gives `error[RAD20033]: Cannot unpack "str" into 2 values` with the v0.7 migration hint. The runtime emission is `core/interpreter.go:1137` inside `runForLoopList`, gated on `vars[0]` being one of `idx` / `index` / `i` / `_` and the element not being a list. The static equivalent belongs in `rts/check/type_check.go:987` `walkForLoop`, which already computes `loopElementType(iterType)` and `mapKeyValTypes(iterType)`. Two vars, a non-map iterable, and a known non-list element type is the same condition, evaluated statically.
- **Over-arity destructuring.** `rts/check/type_check.go:2210` `walkAssign` routes `x, y, z = expr` through `distributeUnpack` (`:2369`). `distributeUnpackArm` (`:2382`) fills every target past a tuple's length with `rl.NewNullType()` and says nothing. That silent null-fill is the hole. When the RHS is a `*rl.TypingTupleT` of known length and there are more targets than elements, the diagnostic belongs right there, at the `i < len(elems)` branch.
- `walkForLoop` also has no arm at all for `len(vars) >= 3` (`rts/check/type_check.go:991-1007` covers only 1 and 2), so three-var loop destructuring is currently both untyped and undiagnosed. That is the `argus` "zip-of-five into six" shape.
- Read `rts/check/snapshots/tuple_unpack.snap` first: it pins what unpack typing currently asserts, including the "targets past the end get null" behavior that will change.
- New 4xxxx codes go in `rts/rl/errors.go`. The highest in use is `ErrIntLiteralOutOfRange = "40015"`; numbers are never reused, and retired codes keep their number with a `_retired` suffix. Each needs `core/error_docs/<code>.md`. For the pre-v0.7 loop shape, decide explicitly whether the static diagnostic reuses `ErrUnpackMismatch` (`rts/rl/errors.go:92`, RAD20033) so check and run say the same thing, or gets its own lint code in the 4xxxx band.
- The contrast the card draws is real: an unresolved name like the removed `get_default` is caught because `rts/check/binder.go` `resolveIdentifier` emits a hard diagnostic on a miss. A wrong-arity destructure has no such rule.

### How to verify

- `make build`, then run `./bin/radd check script.rad` and `./bin/radd script.rad` on the same file and confirm they now agree.
- Checker snapshots: `go test ./rts/check/ -run TestCheckSnapshots -update=tuple_unpack` (the `=` is required; a bare `-update` swallows `-run`). New cases can go in a new `.snap` under `rts/check/snapshots/`.
- The runtime is unchanged, but re-run `go test ./core/testing/ -run TestSnapshots` to confirm nothing regressed.
- `core/testing/docs_snippets_test.go:102` `TestDocSnippets` runs every snippet in `docs-web/docs/` through the checker. A new diagnostic that over-fires on documented code fails there, which is the fastest available over-fire detector.
- `make all`.

### Done when

- `for i, item in ["a", "b"]` produces a check-time diagnostic carrying the same v0.7 migration link the runtime emits.
- Destructuring more targets than a statically-known tuple has produces a diagnostic.
- New codes registered in `rts/rl/errors.go`, documented at `core/error_docs/<code>.md`, `make generate` run, `make verify-generated` clean.
- Snapshot cases for both firing and non-firing shapes, including the legitimate `for k, v in some_map` and a dynamic-RHS unpack that must stay silent.
- No new diagnostics on `docs-web/docs/` snippets.

### Watch out for

- `rts` must not import `core`, so the v0.7 migration hint text has to be written in `rts` rather than imported from the interpreter. Keep the two strings in sync or the check-time and run-time messages will drift.
- The runtime's condition is value-shaped ("this element is not a list"); the checker's is type-shaped. Where the element type is `dynamic` or a union that includes a list, stay silent. A false positive is worse than a miss here, because the sibling card in this column is entirely about the hint tier having lost credibility.
- `core/error_docs/` has its own style guide at `core/error_docs/AGENTS.md`. `docs-web/docs/reference/errors.md` and `core/embedded_docs/` are generated from it.
- Turning previously-clean scripts into failing `rad check` runs is a behavior change users will feel even though no language semantics moved. Consider whether the new diagnostics ship as errors or warnings, and whether they belong in `rts/check/check.go:146` `strictOnlyCodes` for a release before being promoted.
title: Stop rad check certifying scripts that cannot run
